newsitem.title: ITALY: Three Italian aid workers disappear in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Three Italian aid workers disappear in Chechnya.

text.p: Three Italian aid workers disappeared in Chechnya three days ago while on a mission to deliver medicine and equipment to a war-damaged hospital, their aid organisation said in a statement on Sunday.
The non-governmental aid group INTERSOS said it suspected they had been kidnapped.
INTERSOS said in the statement the three men set off by car on September 26 from Nazran in Ingushetia, a region bordering Chechnya, heading for the Chechen capital Grozny.
A colleague raised the alarm when they failed to arrive.
"The most likely hypothesis is that Chechen nationalists kidnapped the car and equipment in order to ask for urgent aid for wounded people in isolated villages," the statement said.
It ruled out a car accident or ambush.
INTERSOS named the three men as Sandro Pocaterra, 41, who had been the group's representative in Chechnya since February and two doctors, Augusto Lombardo, 36, and Giuseppe Valenti, 62.
The Italian foreign ministry said it was working with the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe and other authorities to try to trace them. It had no further details.
